name: Hashing contract broken by hashCode method typo (not overriding Object.hashCode)
description: A class intends to override Object.hashCode() but contains a typo in the method name or signature (for example, hashcode(), hashCode(int), HashCode()). As a result, the override is missing and Java uses Object.hashCode (identity-based). Even if equals is correctly overridden, using the object in hashed collections breaks invariants: equals objects may end up in different hash buckets and lookups fail unpredictably, producing cache misses, duplicate entries, and inconsistent protocol/state comparisons.

trigger_conditions.test_shape: Tests that insert an object into a HashMap/HashSet and later attempt to retrieve it using a logically equal object (or re-constructed object).
trigger_conditions.input_properties: Equals returns true for two distinct instances, but their identity hash codes differ and the class does not provide a proper hashCode override.

example.description: A value-like key (peerId + channelId + sequence) is used to index protocol frames in a HashMap for deduplication and replay protection. equals(Object) is implemented correctly, but a refactor introduces a hashCode typo: hashcode() is defined instead of overriding hashCode(). HashMap therefore uses Object.hashCode (identity), so a logically equal key reconstructed on the next parse hashes to a different bucket and lookups miss, creating duplicate entries and broken state invariants without exceptions.
